abstract: Transcription elongation by RNA polymerase II (RNAPII) requires phosphorylation of the C-terminal repeat (CTR) of the elongation factor Spt5 by the Bur1-Bur2 kinase, yet how this modification is sustained remains unclear. Here we identify the conserved Ran cofactor Mog1 as a positive determinant of Spt5 CTR phosphorylation in budding yeast. Cells lacking Mog1 show reduced Spt5 phosphorylation and chromatin association, lower RNAPII CTD Ser2 phosphorylation and a previously unreported, guanine-reversible sensitivity to nucleotide depletion. These defects are mediated by Spt4, which accumulates in mog1{Delta} cells without a change in its nucleoplasmic distribution, and deleting SPT4 restores Spt5 phosphorylation, H2B monoubiquitination and H3K4 trimethylation, and normal growth and morphology. Both Spt4-Spt5 subunits, but neither BUR kinase subunit, co-purify with Mog1. Deleting the demethylase JHD2 restores H3K4me3 without rescuing growth, establishing the chromatin defects as consequences, not causes, of the elongation defect. Bur1 abundance and activation are unaffected in mog1{Delta} cells, and reducing BUR activity partially compensates rather than aggravates the loss of Mog1, indicating that Mog1 acts on the Spt4-Spt5 substrate; synthetic sickness with ctk1{Delta} places its contribution in early elongation. We propose that Spt4 imposes a limit on Spt5 CTR phosphorylation and that Mog1 counteracts this constraint.
